narrative.title: The Dockhands' XOR Handshake
narrative.scenario: Two dockhands carry pallet tokens and need to trade them, but the dock forbids spare clipboards — no third hand allowed. The XOR handshake saves them: combining their tokens into one register, each worker can re-derive the other's token by XOR-ing the register against what they still hold. Three such handshakes leave every token in the other's grip.
narrative.outputFormat: The pair [b, a] — the values after swapping.

testCases.explanation: Three XOR rounds exchange the values with no third storage slot.
Equal tokens survive the handshake — the swap is its own identity here.

hintLevels: Level 1: XOR is its own inverse — a value XOR-ed with a mask twice returns to itself.
Level 2: Sequence it as a ^= b, then b ^= a (b now holds the old a), then a ^= b (a now holds the old b).
Level 3: The only trap is swapping a variable with itself in-place (a ^= a zeroes it) — distinct variables with equal values are safe.
